/**
 * @name Command injection in numpy core
 * @description Executing system commands with unsanitized user input in numpy core code
 * @kind path-problem
 * @problem.severity error
 * @id py/numpy-core-command-injection
 * @tags security
 *        external/cwe/cwe-078
 */

import python
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.DataFlow
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.TaintTracking
import semmle.python.Concepts
import semmle.python.ApiGraphs

module CommandInjectionConfig implements DataFlow::ConfigSig {
  predicate isSource(DataFlow::Node source) {
    exists(DataFlow::ParameterNode param |
      source = param and
      not param.getParameter().getName() in ["self", "cls"] and
      param.getLocation().getFile().getRelativePath().matches("numpy/%")
    )
  }

  predicate isSink(DataFlow::Node sink) {
    exists(SystemCommandExecution cmd |
      sink = cmd.getCommand() and
      cmd.getLocation().getFile().getRelativePath().matches("numpy/%")
    )
  }
}

module CommandInjectionFlow = TaintTracking::Global<CommandInjectionConfig>;
import CommandInjectionFlow::PathGraph

from CommandInjectionFlow::PathNode source, CommandInjectionFlow::PathNode sink
where CommandInjectionFlow::flowPath(source, sink)
select sink.getNode(), source, sink, "Command injection from $@.", source.getNode(), "user input"
findings.hypothesis: Command injection vulnerabilities in numpy core code where user-controlled parameters flow to system command execution

/**
 * @name Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
 * @description Making HTTP requests to user-controlled URLs can lead to SSRF attacks
 * @kind path-problem
 * @problem.severity error
 * @id py/numpy-ssrf
 * @tags security
 *        external/cwe/cwe-918
 */

import python
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.DataFlow
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.TaintTracking
import semmle.python.ApiGraphs

module SSRFConfig implements DataFlow::ConfigSig {
  predicate isSource(DataFlow::Node source) {
    exists(DataFlow::ParameterNode param |
      source = param and
      param.getParameter().getName() in ["url", "uri", "link", "path", "source"] and
      not param.getParameter().getName() in ["self", "cls"]
    )
  }

  predicate isSink(DataFlow::Node sink) {
    exists(DataFlow::CallCfgNode call |
      (
        call = API::moduleImport("urllib").getMember("request").getMember(["urlopen", "urlretrieve"]).getACall() or
        call = API::moduleImport("urllib").getMember(["request", "urlopen"]).getACall() or
        call = API::moduleImport("requests").getMember(["get", "post", "put", "delete", "request"]).getACall() or
        call = API::moduleImport("http").getMember("client").getMember("HTTPConnection").getACall()
      ) and
      sink = call.getArg(0)
    )
  }
}

module SSRFFlow = TaintTracking::Global<SSRFConfig>;
import SSRFFlow::PathGraph

from SSRFFlow::PathNode source, SSRFFlow::PathNode sink
where 
  SSRFFlow::flowPath(source, sink) and
  sink.getNode().getLocation().getFile().getRelativePath().matches("numpy/%")
select sink.getNode(), source, sink, "SSRF from $@.", source.getNode(), "user-controlled URL"
findings.hypothesis: Server-Side Request Forgery via user-controlled URLs in HTTP requests

/**
 * @name Code injection via eval or exec
 * @description Using eval or exec with user-controlled input can lead to arbitrary code execution
 * @kind path-problem
 * @problem.severity error
 * @id py/numpy-code-injection
 * @tags security
 *        external/cwe/cwe-094
 */

import python
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.DataFlow
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.TaintTracking
import semmle.python.ApiGraphs

module CodeInjectionConfig implements DataFlow::ConfigSig {
  predicate isSource(DataFlow::Node source) {
    exists(DataFlow::ParameterNode param |
      source = param and
      not param.getParameter().getName() in ["self", "cls"]
    )
  }

  predicate isSink(DataFlow::Node sink) {
    exists(DataFlow::CallCfgNode call |
      (
        call = API::builtin("eval").getACall() or
        call = API::builtin("exec").getACall() or
        call = API::builtin("compile").getACall()
      ) and
      sink = call.getArg(0)
    )
  }
}

module CodeInjectionFlow = TaintTracking::Global<CodeInjectionConfig>;
import CodeInjectionFlow::PathGraph

from CodeInjectionFlow::PathNode source, CodeInjectionFlow::PathNode sink
where 
  CodeInjectionFlow::flowPath(source, sink) and
  sink.getNode().getLocation().getFile().getRelativePath().matches("numpy/%") and
  not sink.getNode().getLocation().getFile().getRelativePath().matches("numpy/distutils/%")
select sink.getNode(), source, sink, "Code injection from $@.", source.getNode(), "user input"
findings.hypothesis: Check for code injection vulnerabilities via eval/exec in numpy core code

/**
 * @name Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS)
 * @description Inefficient regular expressions can lead to denial of service
 * @kind problem
 * @problem.severity warning
 * @id py/numpy-redos
 * @tags security
 *        external/cwe/cwe-1333
 */

import python
import semmle.python.ApiGraphs

from DataFlow::CallCfgNode call, string pattern
where
  (
    call = API::moduleImport("re").getMember(["compile", "match", "search", "findall", "finditer", "sub", "subn", "split"]).getACall()
  ) and
  call.getArg(0).asExpr().(StrConst).getText() = pattern and
  (
    // Nested quantifiers
    pattern.regexpMatch(".*[*+]{2,}.*") or
    // Overlapping alternatives
    pattern.regexpMatch(".*(\\|.*){3,}.*") or
    // Catastrophic backtracking patterns
    pattern.regexpMatch(".*\\(.*[*+].*\\)[*+].*")
  ) and
  call.getLocation().getFile().getRelativePath().matches("numpy/%")
select call, "Potentially inefficient regular expression that could lead to ReDoS."
findings.hypothesis: Regular expressions with nested quantifiers or overlapping alternatives can cause exponential backtracking leading to denial of service

  str.getText().length() > 8 and
  not str.getText().matches(["%example%", "%test%", "%dummy%", "%placeholder%", "%your_%", "%<<%", "%>>%"])
select assign, "Potential hardcoded credential or secret."
